question: Explain meta tags in HTML
answerGeneral: Meta tags are `<meta>` elements placed in `<head>` that provide machine-readable metadata about the page — not displayed to users but consumed by browsers, search engines, and social platforms. Key meta tags: `charset` (encoding), `viewport` (responsive layout), `description` (SEO snippet), `robots` (crawler directives), Open Graph (`og:title`, `og:image`) for social sharing, and `http-equiv` for legacy pragma directives. The `name`/`content` pair is the standard format; `charset` and `http-equiv` are special cases with their own syntax.
detailMd:
## Essential meta tags

```html
<head>
  <!-- Encoding — must be first -->
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />

  <!-- Responsive viewport -->
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />

  <!-- SEO description (shown in search snippets) -->
  <meta name="description" content="A concise page description, ideally 150–160 chars." />

  <!-- Crawler directives -->
  <meta name="robots" content="index, follow" />

  <!-- Author -->
  <meta name="author" content="Aaron Kisac" />
</head>
```

## Open Graph (social sharing)

```html
<meta property="og:title"       content="Interview Prep App" />
<meta property="og:description" content="React, TypeScript, Next.js interview questions." />
<meta property="og:image"       content="https://example.com/og.png" />
<meta property="og:url"         content="https://example.com/" />
<meta property="og:type"        content="website" />

<!-- Twitter Card -->
<meta name="twitter:card"  content="summary_large_image" />
<meta name="twitter:title" content="Interview Prep App" />
```

## http-equiv (legacy pragma)

```html
<!-- Content-Security-Policy (prefer HTTP header) -->
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'" />

<!-- Page refresh (avoid — use JS or server redirects) -->
<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="5; url=https://example.com" />
```

## viewport in detail

```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
```

Without this, mobile browsers render pages at ~980 px wide (desktop width) and scale them down — text is tiny and `@media` breakpoints fire at wrong sizes. This is the single most impactful meta tag for responsive design.
answerGeneralTr: Meta etiketler, `<head>` içine yerleştirilen `<meta>` öğeleridir ve sayfa hakkında kullanıcılara gösterilmeyen ancak tarayıcılar, arama motorları ve sosyal platformlar tarafından kullanılan makine tarafından okunabilir meta veriler sağlar. Temel meta etiketler: `charset` (kodlama), `viewport` (duyarlı düzen), `description` (SEO snippeti), `robots` (tarayıcı direktifleri), Open Graph (`og:title`, `og:image`) sosyal paylaşım için ve `http-equiv` eski pragma direktifleri için. `name`/`content` çifti standart formattır; `charset` ve `http-equiv` kendi sözdizimleriyle özel durumlardır.

question: What were some of the key goals and motivations for the HTML5 specification?
answerGeneral: HTML5 was driven by four main goals: (1) **reduce plugin dependency** — provide native APIs for video, audio, canvas drawing, and geolocation so Flash/Silverlight were no longer needed; (2) **better semantics** — introduce elements like `<header>`, `<article>`, `<nav>`, `<section>` so page structure could be machine-readable for accessibility and SEO; (3) **improve forms** — add input types (`email`, `date`, `range`), validation attributes (`required`, `pattern`), and `placeholder` natively; (4) **offline and storage** — localStorage, sessionStorage, AppCache (later replaced by Service Workers), and Web Workers for background threads.

question: What's the difference between an "attribute" and a "property" in HTML?
answerGeneral: **Attributes** are defined in HTML markup and parsed into the initial DOM state — they are always strings (`<input value="hello">`). **Properties** are live JavaScript object properties on the DOM node and reflect the current runtime state. After the user types in an input, `input.value` (property) holds what they typed, while `input.getAttribute('value')` (attribute) still returns the original HTML default. Not all attributes map 1:1 to properties — `class` attribute maps to `className` property; `for` maps to `htmlFor`. Some properties have no attribute counterpart (e.g. `textContent`, `innerHTML`).
detailMd:
## The divergence in action

```html
<input id="name" type="text" value="initial" />
```

```js
const input = document.getElementById('name');

// Before user interaction
console.log(input.getAttribute('value')); // 'initial' — attribute
console.log(input.value);                 // 'initial' — property (synced at parse)

// After user types 'changed' into the field
console.log(input.getAttribute('value')); // still 'initial' — attribute unchanged
console.log(input.value);                 // 'changed' — property reflects current state
```

## Attribute → Property name mapping quirks

| HTML attribute | DOM property |
|---|---|
| `class` | `className` |
| `for` | `htmlFor` |
| `tabindex` | `tabIndex` |
| `readonly` | `readOnly` |
| `maxlength` | `maxLength` |
| `colspan` | `colSpan` |

## Boolean attributes

```html
<!-- Presence = true, absence = false -->
<input disabled />          <!-- disabled attribute present -->
<input />                   <!-- disabled attribute absent -->
```

```js
input.disabled;                    // true / false (property)
input.getAttribute('disabled');    // '' (empty string) or null
input.setAttribute('disabled', ''); // enables it
input.removeAttribute('disabled'); // disables it
```

## React's take

React uses the DOM property names (`className`, `htmlFor`) in JSX — not the HTML attribute names — because JSX compiles to property assignments, not innerHTML parsing.
answerGeneralTr: **Öznitelikler** HTML işaretlemesinde tanımlanır ve ilk DOM durumuna ayrıştırılır — her zaman stringdirler (`<input value="hello">`). **Özellikler**, DOM düğümündeki canlı JavaScript nesnesi özellikleridir ve mevcut çalışma zamanı durumunu yansıtır. Kullanıcı bir input'a yazdıktan sonra, `input.value` (özellik) yazılanı tutarken `input.getAttribute('value')` (öznitelik) hâlâ orijinal HTML varsayılanını döndürür. Tüm öznitelikler 1:1 özelliklere eşleşmez — `class` özniteliği `className` özelliğine eşleşir; `for` ise `htmlFor`'a.

question: What's new in HTML5?
answerGeneral: HTML5 introduced several major additions over HTML4: **semantic elements** (`<header>`, `<footer>`, `<nav>`, `<article>`, `<section>`, `<aside>`, `<main>`); **media elements** (`<video>`, `<audio>`) with native browser controls; **`<canvas>`** for 2D/3D drawing via JavaScript; **improved forms** (new input types, `required`, `placeholder`, `pattern`); **Web Storage** (`localStorage`, `sessionStorage`); **Web Workers** for background threads; **Geolocation API**; **WebSocket API** for real-time communication; **`<picture>`** and `srcset` for responsive images; and **`data-*`** custom attributes.

question: Where and why is the rel="noopener" attribute used?
answerGeneral: `rel="noopener"` is added to `<a target="_blank">` links to prevent the newly opened tab from accessing the opener page via `window.opener`. Without it, a malicious linked page can set `window.opener.location` to redirect the original tab — a phishing attack known as reverse tabnapping. Modern browsers (Chrome 88+) set `noopener` implicitly for `target="_blank"`, but adding it explicitly is still good practice for compatibility. Pair it with `noreferrer` (which implies `noopener` and also omits the `Referer` header) for maximum privacy.
detailMd: ## The vulnerability ```html Read more ``` ```js // Inside attacker.com — can redirect the parent tab! window.opener.location = 'https://attacker.com/phishing-page'; ``` The user sees the original tab replaced by a convincing phishing page while they were reading the new tab. ## The fix ```html Link Link ``` ## Modern browser behaviour Chrome 88+ and Firefox 79+ automatically apply `noopener` to all `target="_blank"` links, making the attack less common. Explicit `rel="noopener noreferrer"` is still recommended for: - Older browser support - Privacy (preventing the `Referer` header from leaking URL information) - Code clarity / linting rules ## ESLint / a11y rules Plugins like `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` flag `target="_blank"` without `rel="noopener noreferrer"` as a warning — you'll see this in most React projects.
answerGeneralTr: `rel="noopener"`, yeni açılan sekmenin `window.opener` aracılığıyla açan sayfaya erişmesini engellemek için `<a target="_blank">` bağlantılarına eklenir. Bu olmadan, kötü amaçlı bir bağlantı sayfası `window.opener.location`'ı orijinal sekmeyi yönlendirmek için ayarlayabilir — bu saldırı 'reverse tabnapping' olarak bilinir. Modern tarayıcılar (Chrome 88+) `target="_blank"` için örtük olarak `noopener` ayarlar, ancak uyumluluk için açıkça eklemek iyi bir pratiktir. `Referer` başlığını da kaldıran `noreferrer` ile birleştirin.

question: What are data-* attributes good for?
answerGeneral: `data-*` attributes let you embed custom data directly in HTML elements without using non-standard attributes or hidden inputs. Any attribute starting with `data-` followed by at least one character is valid. The data is accessible in JavaScript via the `dataset` property, which automatically camelCases hyphenated names. Common uses: storing IDs for JavaScript hooks (`data-user-id`), controlling CSS state without adding/removing classes, and passing config to web components. They are preferable to storing state in `id` or `class` attributes because they have no semantic or styling side effects.
detailMd:
## Setting and reading data-*

```html
<article
  data-user-id="42"
  data-post-type="tutorial"
  data-published="true"
>
  Hello
</article>
```

```js
const article = document.querySelector('article');

// Read — hyphen-to-camelCase automatic
console.log(article.dataset.userId);    // '42'   (always a string)
console.log(article.dataset.postType);  // 'tutorial'
console.log(article.dataset.published); // 'true'

// Write
article.dataset.userId = '99';

// Delete
delete article.dataset.postType;
// or
article.removeAttribute('data-post-type');
```

## Via getAttribute (alternative, no camelCase conversion)

```js
article.getAttribute('data-user-id');       // '42'
article.setAttribute('data-user-id', '99'); // set
```

## CSS access

```css
[data-post-type="tutorial"] { border-left: 4px solid blue; }
```

```css
/* attr() for content in CSS */
article::before { content: attr(data-post-type); }
```

## When NOT to use them

- Do not store large or frequently changing state in data-* — DOM manipulation is slow; use JavaScript variables or state management.
- Do not store sensitive data — data-* is visible in DevTools and accessible to any script on the page.
- Don't use for accessibility semantics — use ARIA attributes (`aria-*`) instead.
answerGeneralTr: `data-*` öznitelikleri, standart olmayan öznitelikler veya gizli girişler kullanmadan doğrudan HTML öğelerine özel veri gömmenizi sağlar. `data-` ile başlayan ve ardından en az bir karakter gelen herhangi bir öznitelik geçerlidir. Veriler JavaScript'te `dataset` özelliği aracılığıyla erişilebilir; bu özellik tire ayrılmış adları otomatik olarak camelCase'e çevirir. Yaygın kullanımlar: JavaScript kancaları için ID depolama, CSS durumunu kontrol etme ve web bileşenlerine config iletme.
